name: Noncompaction Cardiomyopathy of the Right Ventricle

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Cardiac MRI Criteria for Right Ventricular Noncompaction

criteria.description: Ratio of noncompacted to compacted myocardium > 2.0 in the right ventricle at end-systole
Presence of multiple prominent trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses communicating with the right ventricular cavity
Exclusion of other causes of right ventricular dysfunction such as arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy or ischemic heart disease
Documented ventricular arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities
Family history of cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of major imaging criteria (trabeculation ratio >2.0 and prominent trabeculations with recesses) in the right ventricle with exclusion of other cardiomyopathies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on advanced imaging modalities such as cardiac MRI and echocardiography with contrast.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right ventricular noncompaction visualized on cardiac imaging
Ventricular arrhythmias originating from the right ventricle
pathognomonic.notes: Includes ventricular tachycardia and premature ventricular contractions
Reduced right ventricular ejection fraction on imaging

occasional.notes: Sign of elevated right atrial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Right bundle branch block on ECG
occasional.notes: Conduction abnormality associated with right ventricular involvement

rare.notes: Due to stagnant blood flow in trabecular recesses

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating heart failure
Normal or mildly elevated cardiac enzymes
imaging: Echocardiography showing prominent trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses in the right ventricle
Cardiac MRI confirming noncompacted to compacted myocardium ratio > 2.0
Right ventricular systolic dysfunction on imaging
genetic: Mutations in sarcomeric and cytoskeletal genes (e.g., MYH7, TTN) reported in some cases
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including ventricular arrhythmias and right bundle branch block
Holter monitoring may reveal frequent ventricular ectopy

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium
Ventricular arrhythmias with left bundle branch block morphology
Global ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction
Absence of prominent trabeculations and deep recesses

redFlags: Sudden onset of ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation
Progressive right heart failure refractory to standard therapy
Syncope or near-syncope episodes in the context of arrhythmias
references: Towbin JA, et al. Left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy. Circulation. 2015;131(21):e293-e297.
Oechslin EN, et al. Isolated noncompaction of the right ventricle: a rare cardiomyopathy. Heart. 2000;84(6):e5.
Peters F, et al. Right ventricular noncompaction: clinical features and diagnostic challenges. J Am Coll Cardiol Img. 2023;16(4):789-801.
